filo rules [DIR]
filo rules add DIR [PATTERN] POLICY [--dry-run]
filo rules set DIR [PATTERN] POLICY
filo rules remove DIR [PATTERN]

  A rule names a policy for the files under a directory, at any depth, or only
  those whose name matches PATTERN: * is any run of characters, ? one character,
  in any case. Without a pattern it is *. Quote a pattern with * or spaces
  ('*Statement*'), or the shell replaces it with file names.

  A rule sets the policy of a file only if it has no retention at all, and only
  once: a file with a date, forever or a policy (even one with no value) is
  never touched, nor one whose retention you cleared after a rule set it. For a
  file, the rules of its own directory are tried first, then those of each
  directory above it: the first directory with a matching rule decides. In a
  directory, the pattern with the most letters wins (* and ? are not counted);
  two with as many are reported, not guessed.

  filo rules lists them in the order they are tried, with how many files each
  set a policy on, and flags a directory that is gone and a policy with no
  value. add adds a rule and sets the policy of the files it decides now, and
  says how many; a policy that does not exist is created with no value. set
  changes the policy a rule gives from now on: the files it set one on keep
  theirs. remove removes a rule: the files it set a policy on keep it. set and
  remove name the pattern exactly as the rule has it.

Flags
  --dry-run                add: show the files it would set a policy on, and
                           change nothing

  Nothing is asked: a rule only sets a retention. Nothing is deleted except by
  filo delete, which asks.
